officialSources.title: Microsoft Playwright MCP: Connecting to Browsers
claimsUsed: Chrome and Edge channel connection may be enabled in chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging; documented permission is 'Allow remote debugging for this browser instance'.
CDP may connect by endpoint such as http://localhost:9222 or by supported Chrome/Edge channel names.
Playwright Extension attaches to existing tabs and reuses logged-in sessions, cookies and installed extensions; its documented setup uses --extension and can pin a profile with --profile-dir-name.
officialSources.limits: The guide describes supported configuration; it does not guarantee every Chromium fork, browser build, MCP host topology or client-specific setup works unchanged.

officialSources.title: Microsoft Playwright: Playwright Chrome Extension README
claimsUsed: Prerequisite is a Chrome, Edge or Chromium browser; the extension install link points to the Chrome Web Store.
First interaction presents a page for selecting the browser tab; connection approval is required by default.
Clients receive separate tab groups, and the status page can inspect connections and disconnect them individually.
PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXTENSION_TOKEN is profile-specific, displayed in the extension UI, and avoids repeated manual connection approval when configured.
--profile-dir-name selects a profile by the final directory component of Profile Path at chrome://version; the token must match that profile.
Without an explicit profile name, the documented default is the last-used browser profile with the extension installed.
The inspected extension documentation does not describe a token revocation control.
officialSources.limits: Token authenticates the connection; it is not documented as a restriction on subsequent browser actions. No claim is made that a token provides authorization for a website or user account.

officialSources.title: Microsoft Playwright MCP README and configuration
claimsUsed: The server can use a Playwright-managed persistent profile, isolated contexts or an existing browser extension connection.
A persistent profile stores browser data in its user-data directory and one directory cannot be shared by concurrent browser instances.
Isolated mode discards session storage when the browser closes; storage state can be provided separately.
Browsers attached over CDP or extension are not automatically closed; an idle timeout disconnects from externally owned browsers while pages remain open.
officialSources.limits: Mode descriptions are kept distinct from promises about any specific MCP client or vendor-managed browser.

officialSources.title: Chrome for Developers: Changes to remote debugging switches
claimsUsed: Chrome 136 changed remote debugging switch behavior and requires a non-default user-data directory for the documented remote-debugging scenario.
officialSources.limits: The article avoids presenting older launch commands as universally current and does not generalize Chromium-fork behavior beyond the cited Chrome guidance.

practicalChecksIncluded: Pick the connection mode before configuring a browser.
Pin the extension to the intended Chrome profile and verify the selected tab and signed-in account before actions.
Keep CDP local or behind deliberate access controls and use a dedicated test user-data directory.
Troubleshoot missing tabs, repeated approval, CDP refusal or timeout, wrong profile/tab, and browser processes that remain open after disconnect.
Disconnect extension clients and remove temporary tokens and configuration according to the profile's data-retention policy.
